result.title: Map-Distribution Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
result.summary: Designing capable neural policies for multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF), which map local observations to action distributions, represents an important challenge in multi-agent learning, with practical relevance to scalable collective automation problems such as warehouse logistics. In contrast to prior studies focusing primarily on individual policy design, this study explores a meta-level Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approach to learning-based MAPF. Specifically, given a collection of compact yet high-performing experts specialised for different map distributions, our architecture learns a router that selectively fuses their outputs according to each agent's local situation. We instantiate and validate this MoE approach with a commonly used graph neural network-based policy as well as a newly developed recursive action-token refinement model. Combined with supervised and reinforcement learning fine-tuning of the experts, our experiments show that MoE generally improves upon the pretrained policy and outperforms existing leading methods. At the same time, our findings reveal that appropriately trained, parameter-matched monolithic models still outperform MoE, highlighting a nuanced role for map-distribution MoE for MAPF.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多智能体路径规划（MAPF）中的神经策略，提出一种元层面的 Map-Distribution MoE：先训练面向不同地图分布的紧凑专家，再学习路由器按各智能体的局部情境选择性融合专家输出，并配合监督与强化学习微调，以图神经网络策略和新提出的递归动作 token 精化模型作为实例验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「递归动作 token 精化」与「按局部情境路由并融合专家输出」可能为 LVR 的迭代状态更新与动态计算选择提供方法线索，另需核查其「参数匹配的单体模型仍优于 MoE」的结论是否提示路由式组合存在收益边界。
